For Respondent(s) : Mr. Dhanpat Choudhary
 Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Madan Gopal Vyas
Judgment 17/10/2023

The instant civil miscellaneous appeal under Section 173, Motor Vehicles Act is directed against the award dated 14.07.2009 passed by the learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Banswara (hereinafter referred to as the learned Tribunal) in Claim Case no. 295/2006 whereby the claim application filed by the claimant- appellant under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act (for short hereinafter called; "MV Act") was allowed in part and compensation to the tune of Rs. 64,000/- with interest @ 6% per annum was granted.
2. Learned counsel for the appellant-claimant submits that the learned Tribunal has grossly erred in awarding a meager compensation of Rs. 64,000/-.
It is further submitted that the learned Tribunal has failed to consider the evidence available on record with respect to the intensive medical treatment of the claimant.

It is submitted that the claimant underwent a long [2023:RJ-JD:35479]
(2 of 3) [CMA-3438/2011] medical treatment and huge amount of money was spent on the same.
It is further submitted that the compensation under the head of 'Transportation and Attendent" is also very less as the appellant was referred by the doctor to another hospital.
Thus, it is prayed that the award passed by the learned Tribunal be enhanced.
3. Per contra, learned counsel representing the respondent no. 2-Insurance Company opposed the prayer of enhancement of award amount made by learned counsel for appellant.

sentences.text: 1 4. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the material available on record.
5. A bare perusal of judgment and award dated 14.07.2009 shows that the learned Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs. 3000/- under the head of medical expenses.
Further, Rs 6000/- has been granted for attendant charges and Rs. 5000/- have been granted for transportation charges.

The appellant-claimant has suffered a permanent disability of 50%.
6.

After hearing learned counsel for the parties and looking to the head injury as received due to which the appellant-claimant remained hospitalized for about one month, in my considered opinion, it is a fit case for enhancement of the compensation.
The compensation is enhanced by Rs 50,000/- lump sum.
7. Consequently, the present appeal is allowed.

The impugned award dated 14.07.2009 passed by the learned tribunal is [2023:RJ-JD:35479] (3 of 3) [CMA-3438/2011] modified and the appellant-claimant is held entitled to an additional lump sum amount of Rs. 50,000/- including interest.
The respondent-Insurance Company is directed to pay the amount to the appellant-claimant within two months from today.
8. No order as to costs.

(MADAN GOPAL VYAS),J 33-CPG/-
